# AnimatedVisualPlayer

Header: `winui/ui/media/AnimatedVisualPlayer.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/media/AnimatedVisualPlayer.hpp`.

Plays a caller-supplied [AnimatedVisualSource](../rendering/animated-visual-source.md) by advancing its progress over time and drawing each frame with the source's render_frame().

With [auto_play()](#auto_play) on (the default), a newly loaded source starts looping from 0 to 1 at once. Otherwise the app calls [play()](#play), [pause()](#pause), [resume()](#resume), [stop()](#stop) or [set_progress()](#set_progress). A play from `from` to `to` lasts [`duration() * (to - from)`](#duration), scaled by [playback_rate()](#playback_rate) while it runs. A negative rate plays backwards. The source is fitted into the player's bounds as [stretch()](#stretch) says. When the source can't be shown (its `available()` is false), the fallback content takes its place. The player doesn't own the source, so it must outlive the player.

A play keeps running in real time while the player is off screen, scrolled out of view or clipped away, but nothing is drawn and the window isn't kept busy for it. Back on screen, the player shows the progress the play has reached by then, with a looped play wrapped around. A play that ends off screen still completes on time.

Example: 
```cpp
// A source drawing a circle that grows over one second.
struct Pulse final : ui::AnimatedVisualSource
{
    ui::Size natural_size() const override { return {48.0f, 48.0f}; }
    ui::Duration duration() const override { return ui::Duration{1000.0}; }
    void render_frame(ui::Renderer& r, const ui::Rect& b, double progress) const override
    {
        const float radius = static_cast<float>(progress) * b.width / 2.0f;
        r.fill_ellipse(b.center(), radius, radius, ui::colors::Black);
    }
};
static const Pulse pulse; // outlives every player showing it

ui::Control<ui::AnimatedVisualPlayer> player;
window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{
    .content = {
        ui::AnimatedVisualPlayer{.source = &pulse, .auto_play = false, .width = 96.0f,
                                 .height = 96.0f, .control = player,
                                 .fallback_content = ui::Text{.text = "(no animation)"}},
        ui::Button{.text = "Play once", .on_click = [&] { player->play(0.0, 1.0, false); }},
        ui::Button{.text = "Pause", .on_click = [&] { player->pause(); }},
    },
});
```

## `ui::AnimatedVisualPlayer`

A player for a caller-supplied [AnimatedVisualSource](../rendering/animated-visual-source.md) (render/AnimatedVisualSource.hpp). Builds a [ui::AnimatedVisualPlayerControl](#uianimatedvisualplayercontrol).

[`source`](#uianimatedvisualplayer-source) is a non-owning pointer, so the [AnimatedVisualSource](../rendering/animated-visual-source.md) must outlive the built control. Changing the source, through a binding or set_source() on the control, stops the player. [`fallback_content`](#uianimatedvisualplayer-fallback_content) shows instead when the source can't be shown.

Example: 
```cpp
extern const ui::AnimatedVisualSource& logo; // the app's own subclass, alive as long as the window
ui::Control<ui::AnimatedVisualPlayer> player;

window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{.spacing = 8, .content = {
    ui::AnimatedVisualPlayer{.source           = &logo,
                             .auto_play        = false,
                             .width            = 400.0f,
                             .height           = 400.0f,
                             .control          = player,
                             .fallback_content = ui::Text{.text = "Animation unavailable"}},
    ui::HorizontalStack{.spacing = 8, .content = {
        ui::Button{.text = "Play",  .on_click = [&] { player->play(0.0, 1.0, true); }},
        ui::Button{.text = "Pause", .on_click = [&] { player->pause(); }},
        ui::Button{.text = "Stop",  .on_click = [&] { player->stop(); }},
    }},
}});
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::AnimatedVisualPlayer{
    .source, .auto_play, .playback_rate, .stretch, .style, .margin, .width, .height,
    .min_width, .min_height, .max_width, .max_height, .horizontal_alignment,
    .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip, .accessibility, .on_pointer_entered,
    .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus, .on_key_down, .on_wheel, .control,
    .fallback_content
}
```

Fields, in declaration order (designators must follow it):

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="uianimatedvisualplayer-source"></span>`source` | `ui::Binding<const ui::AnimatedVisualSource*>` |  | The animation. Not owned, so it must outlive the built control. |
| <span id="uianimatedvisualplayer-auto_play"></span>`auto_play` | `ui::Binding<bool>` | `{true}` | Whether the whole animation loops as soon as the source loads. |
| <span id="uianimatedvisualplayer-playback_rate"></span>`playback_rate` | `ui::Binding<double>` | `{1.0}` | Playback speed. 1 is normal speed, and a negative rate plays backwards. |
| <span id="uianimatedvisualplayer-stretch"></span>`stretch` | `ui::Binding<ui::Stretch>` | `{ui::Stretch::Uniform}` | How the animation fills the player's box. |
| <span id="uianimatedvisualplayer-on_pointer_entered"></span>`on_pointer_entered` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer moved onto the control. |
| <span id="uianimatedvisualplayer-on_pointer_exited"></span>`on_pointer_exited` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer left the control. |
| <span id="uianimatedvisualplayer-on_got_focus"></span>`on_got_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus arrived on the control, or on anything inside it, from outside it. A control with nothing focusable in it never gets focus, and never raises this. |
| <span id="uianimatedvisualplayer-on_lost_focus"></span>`on_lost_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus left the control and everything inside it. |
| <span id="uianimatedvisualplayer-on_key_down"></span>`on_key_down` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::KeyEvent&)>` |  | A key pressed while focus is on the control or inside it, before the control's own handling; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_key_down()](../tree/element.md#on_key_down)). |
| <span id="uianimatedvisualplayer-on_wheel"></span>`on_wheel` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::PointerEvent&)>` |  | A wheel turn over the control, before the control scrolls; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_wheel()](../tree/element.md#on_wheel)). |
| <span id="uianimatedvisualplayer-control"></span>`control` | `ui::ControlOut<ui::AnimatedVisualPlayer>` |  | Out: the handle that receives the built control. |
| <span id="uianimatedvisualplayer-fallback_content"></span>`fallback_content` | `ui::Spec` |  | Shown instead of the animation when the source can't be shown. |

Plus the common fields `style`, `margin`, `width`, `height`, `min_width`, `min_height`, `max_width`, `max_height`, `horizontal_alignment`, `vertical_alignment`, `visible`, `tool_tip`, `accessibility` every spec carries ([conventions](../conventions.md#common-fields-on-every-spec)).

### build

```cpp
std::unique_ptr<Element> build()&&
```

Consumes the spec and returns the built [ui::AnimatedVisualPlayerControl](#uianimatedvisualplayercontrol); the caller owns it.

## `ui::AnimatedVisualPlayerControl`

Derives from `ui::Panel`.

Plays a caller-supplied [AnimatedVisualSource](../rendering/animated-visual-source.md) by advancing its progress over time and drawing each frame with the source's render_frame().

With [auto_play()](#auto_play) on (the default), a newly loaded source starts looping from 0 to 1 at once. Otherwise the app calls [play()](#play), [pause()](#pause), [resume()](#resume), [stop()](#stop) or [set_progress()](#set_progress). A play from `from` to `to` lasts [`duration() * (to - from)`](#duration), scaled by [playback_rate()](#playback_rate) while it runs. A negative rate plays backwards. The source is fitted into the player's bounds as [stretch()](#stretch) says. When the source can't be shown (its `available()` is false), the fallback content takes its place. The player doesn't own the source, so it must outlive the player.

A play keeps running in real time while the player is off screen, scrolled out of view or clipped away, but nothing is drawn and the window isn't kept busy for it. Back on screen, the player shows the progress the play has reached by then, with a looped play wrapped around. A play that ends off screen still completes on time.

```cpp

{
    ui::Size natural_size() const override { return {48.0f, 48.0f}; }
```

### AnimatedVisualPlayerControl

```cpp
AnimatedVisualPlayerControl() = default
```

A player with no source: auto-play on, rate 1, Uniform stretch.

### source

```cpp
const AnimatedVisualSource* source() const
```

The source being played, or null.

### set_source

```cpp
void set_source(const AnimatedVisualSource* source)
```

Sets the source to play. The player doesn't own it, so the source must outlive the player. Replacing the source stops whatever was playing, and auto-play then starts on the new one. nullptr unloads it. Shows or hides the fallback content as the source's `available()` says.

### is_animated_visual_loaded

```cpp
bool is_animated_visual_loaded() const
```

A source is set, available and has a size.

### set_fallback_content

```cpp
Element* set_fallback_content(std::unique_ptr<Element> content)
```

Sets what shows instead when the source can't be shown. Takes ownership, returns a non-owning observer and replaces any earlier fallback.

### fallback_content

```cpp
Element* fallback_content() const
```

The fallback content (whether or not it is showing), or null if none was set.

### is_fallen_back

```cpp
bool is_fallen_back() const
```

Whether the fallback content is what is showing.

### auto_play

```cpp
bool auto_play() const
```

Whether a loaded source starts looping 0..1 on its own. Default true.

### set_auto_play

```cpp
void set_auto_play(bool auto_play)
```

Turns auto-play on or off. Turning it on while a source is loaded and nothing plays starts the looping play at once.

### playback_rate

```cpp
double playback_rate() const
```

How fast plays run, 1 by default. A negative rate plays backwards.

### set_playback_rate

```cpp
void set_playback_rate(double rate)
```

Sets the playback rate. A running play speeds up, slows down or reverses at once.

### stretch

```cpp
Stretch stretch() const
```

How the source's natural size fits the player's bounds. Uniform by default.

### set_stretch

```cpp
void set_stretch(Stretch stretch)
```

Sets the stretch. Updates layout and redraws.

### is_playing

```cpp
bool is_playing() const
```

Whether a play has started and not completed. A paused play counts as playing.

### is_paused

```cpp
bool is_paused() const
```

Whether the current play is paused.

### progress

```cpp
double progress() const
```

The current position in the animation, from 0 to 1.

### duration

```cpp
Duration duration() const
```

0 until a source is loaded, then the source's [duration()](#duration).

### play

```cpp
void play(double from_progress, double to_progress, bool looped)
```

Completes any play in progress, rewinding it, then plays from `from_progress` to `to_progress`, repeating forever when `looped` is true. Without a loaded source the play waits and doesn't start, and setting a source cancels it.

### pause

```cpp
void pause()
```

Pauses the current play where it is. Does nothing when nothing is playing.

### resume

```cpp
void resume()
```

Continues a paused play. Does nothing when nothing is playing.

### stop

```cpp
void stop()
```

Completes the current play and rewinds [progress()](#progress) to 0. Does nothing when nothing is playing.

### set_progress

```cpp
void set_progress(double progress)
```

Completes any play and jumps to [`progress`](#progress), clamped to [0,1].

### on_screen_changed

```cpp
void on_screen_changed(bool on_screen) override
```

When the player comes back on screen, draws the progress the play reached while away.

### automation_role

```cpp
AutomationRole automation_role() const override
```

Exposed to UI Automation as an image.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

Fits the source's natural size into `available` as [stretch()](#stretch) says, or measures the fallback.

### arrange_override

```cpp
void arrange_override(const Rect& final_rect, const ArrangeContext& context) override
```

Arranges the fallback content when it is showing.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

Draws the source's frame at [progress()](#progress), clipped for UniformToFill, or draws the fallback.

### tick_override

```cpp
void tick_override(Duration delta) override
```

Advances the current play by [`delta * playback_rate()`](#playback_rate), and completes or loops it at its ends. Off screen it draws nothing and keeps the window idle, and a play that ends there still completes on time.
